This is a recommendation and evidence index, **not acceptance**. Inspection is bound to `09d7623e9ea1e7354627d9d5c880bde6eb94bbe9` on 2026-09-26. The active registry remains legacy. No model calls, tests of product behavior, source activation, publication or real-machine operations were performed for this preparation.

The first50 selected files matched that HEAD at initial inspection. Test source is explicitly labeled as source, not a new passing run. [package-obligations.json](package-obligations.json) is direct output from the production `derivePackageAcceptanceObligations`; no criterion decisions are inserted.

The earlier evidence map E02 remains useful but its frontend running-state text is historical. The newer closed frontend report E11 controls that state: the original 66 captures completed, yet the comparison did not qualify. The separate mobile six-attempt qualification E40/E41 has closed, exit0, per the parent update. Parent reports its first repaired candidate still fails the supplied Georgia app-label requirement; this is not a committed full-batch assessment or passing evidence. Parent then applied the exact reviewed patch to inactive E51 and refreshed its E24 derivedDigest. ## Mobile scope decision required by the evidence

The specification does not explicitly permit adopting a failing mapped mobile contract merely by documenting generation fidelity limits:

- Group C, lines 290–302 of E01, preserves image-only mobile behavior and allows honest reporting of missing capability or incompatible parameters. This allows a truthful unavailable/limited result; it does not state that a failed preservation case counts as passed.
- Lines 304–321 require settled brand/content constraints, give existing brand precedence over preset typography, require mobile/brand preservation trials, and permit retirement only after mapped cases pass and safe migration is available.
- AC-10 at line 517 requires brand/image-only/mobile cases to pass. Group B's matched-trial rules, imported by Group C, require every required case and frozen quality floor; lines 267–268 require revise/retest or retained baseline rather than relaxing a failed criterion.
- Lines 587–600 distinguish expressly permitted experimental baseline retention from mandatory capability migration. Retaining existing behavior or delaying the affected package is allowed; calling mandatory migration an optional experiment to declare completion is not.

Exact `1179×2556` and maximum two generation calls are concrete frozen benchmark choices, not numeric requirements written in the governing specification. The installed interface diagnosis E14 establishes no numeric model-facing size parameter and auto sizing, not a universal provider impossibility. A separately frozen native-portrait qualification can test supported mobile image behavior while preserving the original exact-size failure. E40 makes that scope explicit. In contrast, failure to honor the supplied Georgia brand in app-owned labels is directly relevant to the specification's brand-preservation requirement; truthful disclosure is useful but does not repair the pixels or satisfy that check.

After the fixed six close, parent should either establish qualifying mapped evidence, retain the existing contributor/delay the affected frontend migration, or seek an explicit concrete scope amendment from the user if constrained image concepts with known brand-fidelity limits are the desired product. Such an amendment must state the changed guarantee, what remains available, failed evidence, retirement consequences and new acceptance boundary. It cannot be inferred from the earlier preference for optional packages. No partial frontend adoption or automatic retirement is recommended here.

## Final assembly sequence and pitfalls

1. Close the fixed mobile review and make the substantive frontend decision first. Preserve Group B retained baseline, all original failures and bounded presentation/runtime limits. Parent must decide whether unresolved presentation defects affect broader requirements rather than flattening scoped assessments into full passes.
2. Once relevant adoption gates qualify, coherently apply final target registry, source/provenance/profile decisions, retained PS transition payload, documentation and chosen breaking-release version. Regenerate all projections and indexes. Keep immutable original PS3.8 payload/version as the explicit transition exception; all target release manifests/lockfile agree. A same-name changed payload with the same version is rejected by the native caller.
3. Run required sync/check/full tests and available strict Claude validators against those exact bytes, then actual isolated final Codex/Pi discovery and selected package/runtime/closure checks. Existing 462-test/rehearsal evidence is historical. Do not repeat unrelated behavioral experiments; review changed-body/helper/tail bindings and rerun only affected evidence as necessary.
4. Assemble the actual reviewed audit with the exact derived obligations. E22 requires nonempty evidence for every criterion/check, exact check-key equality, full capability/source/criterion equality and original regular evidence files. Only AC-08/09 may use `retained-baseline`; AC-10 cannot. Source entries use `captureMigrationPath().contentSha256` for the exact file/directory, **not** this index's raw-file SHA256 or a guessed recursive hash. Directory bindings detect added/removed files. Raw referenced evidence uses SHA256 of the regular file. Unresolved selected-package checks block activation. The production builder captures all six target projections before selected acceptance; delaying optional frontend exposure does not by itself remove that artifact prerequisite. This machine’s equivalent existing selection includes frontend, so retaining it leaves part of the requested migration unfinished.
5. Commit/integrate the audited sources and evidence before production planning. E23 rejects untracked/dirty audit, source and referenced evidence, and checks HEAD remains fixed during verification. The audit need not contain its own final commit hash: runtime verification supplies actual release HEAD/version/full package digest to an in-memory receipt. Do not create circular self-hashes or hand-author machine proofs. Verify local/released Git tree and payload identity at the final revision; later generator, metadata, provenance or evidence changes require affected rebinding.
6. Distinguish the AC-24 **pre-rollout gate** from the **post-rollout outcome**. The audit may record a genuinely reviewed gate and exact isolated prerequisites; it cannot claim that the still-future publication or actual-machine update already succeeded. Preserve separate final publication/rollout records and do not report goal completion until they are independently observed. Parent owns that criterion wording and decision.
7. Publish only to origin through the authorized release flow, then use the final verified source to observe and plan the real saved/equivalent selection. Codex requires the exact local marketplace registration; no implicit fully unconfigured bootstrap exists. Pi direct-checkout sources can change live exposure when projections change, before a later native CLI call: preserve the retained old PS payload and explicitly control publication/checkout/withdrawal ordering. Do not claim changed working-tree bytes are the old installed baseline. Keep unrelated themes/vendor packages/settings and partial selections intact.
8. Under the per-home lock, stage outside discovery, revalidate bindings, withdraw only proven owned old identities and aliases before exposing replacements, save selection last, retain durable journal/backups and inspect actual final model-visible discovery. Unknown/modified bytes conflict rather than being deleted. Report exact residuals on failure; existing authority permits rollout, not arbitrary recovery. Publication without verified machine outcome is partial completion.

Four preparation passes: inventory current records; inspect criterion semantics and production obligations; challenge failure/fallback/circular-binding claims; verify written references and reproducible pure derivation. No additional model or product test run was needed for this evidence preparation.

Observation amendment: the first G1 binding check correctly failed after the parent changed provenance during preparation. It was not a behavioral failure. The original E24 hash remains recorded; current E24/E51 bytes were rebound transparently. The acceptance state remains unresolved.
